author: reek
body: The PCB board data model. Everything that lives on a physical PCB layout: board outline, copper tracks, vias, zones, placed footprints, and the ratsnest of unrouted connections. All coordinates are in nanometers. Layer IDs follow the KiCad convention: 0 = F.Cu through 31 = B.Cu for copper, with higher IDs for technical layers.

author: reek
body: The board outline is a closed or open polygon of vertices defining the physical edge of the PCB. The edge-cuts layer geometry determines the board shape for manufacturing.

author: reek
body: A track segment is a straight copper trace between two points on a single layer. Width is in nanometers. The locked flag prevents the router from modifying this segment.

author: reek
body: Vias connect copper on different layers. Through vias span the entire stack. Blind vias connect an outer layer to an inner layer. Buried vias connect two inner layers. Micro vias connect adjacent layers only, typically for HDI designs.

author: reek
body: Zones define copper fill areas on a layer. The fill algorithm floods the zone polygon with copper, respecting clearance to other nets. Thermal relief controls how pads connect to the zone pour: direct connection for low impedance or spoke-based relief for easier soldering.

author: reek
body: A placed footprint is a component body positioned on the board. The reference designator links back to the schematic netlist. Layer ID 0 means front copper, 31 means back copper. Pads carry their own net assignments from the netlist.

author: reek
body: The ratsnest is the set of unrouted connections. Each line represents a direct connection that needs a physical copper path. The router converts ratsnest lines into tracks and vias. An empty ratsnest means the board is fully routed.

author: reek
body: The top-level board record. Holds the complete physical PCB design: outline, all copper geometry, placed components, and unrouted connections. Width and height are the bounding box in nanometers. Grid size controls snap resolution.
